ConnectionStrings.//DefaultConnection: The database this API serves from. LEAVE THIS EMPTY HERE — this file is committed to a public repository, and it held the live production credentials until 2026-09-19. It comes from Key Vault in Azure (app setting 'ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection'), from the server's own appsettings.Production.json on MyASP.NET, and from appsettings.Development.json for a local database. The API refuses to start without it rather than falling back to a published value.

Jwt.//Key: The key this API signs and validates every token with. LEAVE THIS EMPTY HERE — this file is committed to a public repository. It comes from Key Vault in Azure (app setting 'Jwt__Key') and from User Secrets on a development machine: dotnet user-secrets set "Jwt:Key" "<a long random value>". The API refuses to start without it rather than falling back to a published value, because a forged token is indistinguishable from a real one.

GoogleMaps.//ApiKey: Server-side key for Routes API and Geocoding API. LEAVE THIS EMPTY HERE. The real value goes in User Secrets in development and an environment variable in production (GoogleMaps__ApiKey) — this file is versioned. It must be a NEW key, restricted in Cloud Console to those two APIs and to this server's IP: the key the Desktop and Driver apps carry is published in a repository and inside a distributed APK, and it is being retired.

Operations.//DefaultTimeZone: Timezone a trip is operated in when its provider has not declared one. A trip at 09:15 is 09:15 at the pickup address, whoever is looking and wherever this is hosted. IANA identifier; .NET accepts these on Windows and Linux alike. The API refuses to start if the host does not recognise it: falling back to the server's own timezone is the defect this setting exists to prevent.
Operations.//BrokerProviderId: Provider row that stands for the broker's own operation. A trip with no ProviderId is one the broker runs itself and takes this provider's timezone.

Realtime.//DriverRoleIds: Roles that connect from Raphael.Driver. Everyone else is treated as a dispatch office user and joins the shared broadcast. Leave empty and nobody does, which keeps office notices private at the cost of Raphael.Desktop receiving nothing.

Cors.//AllowedOrigins: Browser origins allowed to call this API: scheme and host, no trailing slash, one entry per host a page is actually served from ('www' and the bare domain are two origins). Only browsers are governed by this — Desktop and Driver send no Origin header. localhost:8081 is the Expo Metro bundler and localhost:19006 is Expo on the web, both for developing the rider app. The API refuses to start outside Development if this is empty: credentials are allowed, so '*' is illegal and an empty list authorises nobody, which reaches a user as a CORS error that names no cause.

ClientCompatibility.//MinimumVersions: Oldest version of each client application this API expects to serve, keyed by what the application sends in 'X-Client-App'. A client below its floor is answered normally and marked with 'X-Raphael-Client-Status: outdated' plus the floor in 'X-Raphael-Client-Minimum'. It is never refused: leaving a driver mid-route with an app that will not load is worse than anything an old version gets wrong. Raise a floor the day that release is actually in people's hands, not the day its server code was written; an app left empty or absent here is never reported as outdated. The versions below are what _meta/RELEASES.md records as distributed.
